❯ Without using any tools, write about 600 words of plain   
  prose on the history of canals.                           
  
⏺ People have been digging canals for about as long as they
  have been farming. The earliest ones were for irrigation,
  not transport. In Mesopotamia, from about the sixth
  millennium BCE, farmers cut channels from the Tigris and
  Euphrates to carry water to their fields. The
  civilizations of Sumer and Babylon depended on that water,
  and so did their governments. Keeping the channels clear
  and settling disputes over water became central jobs of
  the state. Some historians argue that managing large
